findings.message: The compliance blocker is fixed for `evidence_bundle.contents`, but `keep` still marks a column as safe even though it can hold a person. `delivery.proposal.meta` is kept as 'front matter … its owner is owner_name'. But the sync service accepts `meta: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (services.ts:203) and stores whatever the repo's front matter has (services.ts:273-279). Nothing stops an owner, author or reviewer key from landing there, so erasure and anonymisation never reach it. Fix: either reduce `meta` to a fixed list of keys with no person in them (sha, pr, verdict, withdrawn) before storing it, or move `meta` from `keep` to `fields`.
findings.scenario: A repo's change.md has front matter `author: Nimal Silva`. sync_proposal stores it in meta. Nimal's erasure request completes. delivery.proposal.owner_name is anonymised, but meta.author still reads 'Nimal Silva'.

findings.message: `bundleState` treats any bundle whose contents is `{}` as anonymised and returns `signatureValid: null`. Nothing records that an anonymise actually ran. So a bundle tampered to `{}` now reads as 'anonymised' instead of 'tampered'. That is evidence loss passed off as a known state. Fix: decide 'anonymised' from a marker the retention engine writes (for example `generated_by` anonymised, or an anonymised_at or audit entry). Report `{}` contents without that marker as signature invalid. Add the tamper-to-{} case to the registers test.
findings.scenario: Someone with DB access runs `update compliance.evidence_bundle set contents='{}'` on a bundle that hasn't expired. get_evidence_bundle returns `{anonymised:true, signatureValid:null}` instead of `signatureValid:false`.

findings.message: This round made `userFacing` the app's single rule for which errors a caller may read. But the new refusal `guardShown` throws a plain `Error`, so `userFacing` rejects it. The REST API (rest.ts:18) turns it into a 500 'internal' with a reference. Bulk and other reporters hide its message the same way. The same applies to the new plain `Error`s in the suggestion undo (suggestions.ts: 'that entry is already gone' / 'that week was submitted since'). Fix: throw these through `refuse(...)` from card.ts, which throws `ToolError(…, 'invalid_input')`, and assert the REST status in the test.
findings.scenario: A REST POST to correct_time_entry with `{entryId, hours:1, hoursBefore:2}` on an entry that has 1.5 h returns 500 `{error:'internal'}` instead of 400 with 'the entry changed since you saw it (hoursBefore is 1.5)'.

findings.message: Partly fixed. The new e2e drives the real credentials server action, `cookies()` and the signIn event. The Entra path is still only tested by calling `config.events.signIn` with a hand-built `account: { amax }`. Nothing proves two things: that Auth.js passes the same `account` object to `events.signIn` after `callbacks.signIn` mutates it (authjs.ts:120), and that `cookies()` in the `/api/auth/callback/<entra>` route handler still sees the earlier session cookie. If either is wrong, every test passes and an Entra switch leaves the old session alive. Fix: run one Entra callback through the Auth.js handler against a mocked token/userinfo endpoint, with an earlier session cookie, and assert that the earlier session row has ended.
findings.scenario: An @auth/core upgrade copies `account` before the events run. `account.amax` is then undefined in events.signIn, so the stamp is undefined and nothing is ended. switch.test.ts and the demo e2e both stay green.

findings.message: After retention anonymises a request, its `before` becomes `{}`. `values()` then reads it as `hours: 0, billable: false`, so lost data shows up as real values. changeText and the decide card would show '0 h → 4 h'. Fix: return an explicit anonymised flag, or null hours, and have changeText say 'anonymised' instead of printing 0.
findings.scenario: An anonymised request with `before = {}` → get_change_requests returns `before.hours: 0`, and the card reads 'Hours 0 h → …'.

findings.message: `scopeSql` is a second copy of `chainFor`'s rules, written in SQL. Today they match, and the `reviews()` post-filter catches anything extra. But if a new chain rule is added only to chainFor (a delegate, an entity scope), the SQL never fetches those rows, and approvers lose requests without any error. Fix: derive both from one rule (for example, have chainFor list the inputs scopeSql uses), or add a test that checks the two agree across viewer kinds.

The round-2 finding asked for a check on every text and json column of a table about people. This fix only extends a list of column names (`FREE_TEXT`), so it is an instance fix. Any free-text column whose name is not on the list still passes: `title`, `subject`, `content`, `label`, `topic`, `outcome`, `memo`. Examples already in the repo are a sales task's `title` and an incident's `title`, both of which people write names into. The previous finding also asked to cover tables that have a retention entry but whose person columns are not named like personal columns; `aboutPeople` still leaves those out. Fix: in a table that has a retention entry or a person/user id, use the column type (`text`, `varchar`, `character varying`, `json`, `jsonb`, `text[]`) and require each such column to appear in fields, subject, subjectName or keep. Add `title text` and `varchar` cases to the ac7-config table.
findings.scenario: Migration `alter table people.visit add column title text` on a table with `visitor_email` and a retention entry that does not list `title` → the check passes, and `title` (for example "Visit by Kamal Perera") is never erased or anonymised.

findings.message: The new e2e test drives a real credentials (demo) sign-in through Next's `cookies()` and Auth.js's `signIn` event, which fixes that half of the round-2 B2 finding. The Entra path is still covered only by the hand-built message in `switch.test.ts`. That path depends on `callbacks.signIn` putting `amax` on `account` before `events.signIn` fires during `/api/auth/callback/<entra-id>`. Fix: add one callback test against a mocked token endpoint, or record that this is deferred.
